sentences.text:
Brief facts of the case :
1. The accused has been facing trial of the charge that on 23.05.2018 in between 10:30 p.m. to 11:00 p.m., he stabbed the injured Ritika by sword FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC causing grievous injury with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that if by that act he had caused the death of injured Ritika, he would have been guilty of murder and also intimidated the complainant as well as injured Ritika by threatening to kill the injured Ritika.
Investigation conducted and statement of injured:
2. On 24.05.2018, on receipt of DD No. 5A regarding MLC No. 124146, IO along with HC reached at Safdarjang Hospital and as per the MLC doctor declared the patient Ms. Reetika D/o.
Lt. Kailash "Unfit for giving statement".

State vs Hari Kant Mann on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79732368/
1

IO met the eye-witness Smt. Kavita Giri W/o. Lt. Kailash at Safdarjung Hospital and recorded his statement wherein she stated that she has two children namely Abhishek and Reetika and her daughter was having relations with Harikant Maan for last five years and Harikant was in visiting terms in her house.
She alleged that on 23.05.2018 at about 7:00 p.m., Harikant Maan came to her house to meet her daughter and after sometime, he left.
She alleged that between 9.30pm to 10.30pm, Harikant again came to her house to meet Reetika.
Her daughter Reetika leaving her cousin Divya in bedroom started talking to Harikant Maan in Varandha.

House of the door was opened and after sometime, on hearing quarrel noise between accused Harikant Maan and her daughter Reetika, she went to the door and saw that accused Harikant Maan @ Aashu stabbed her daughter Reetika on her abdomen with a sword type weapon and threatened her and run away from the spot.
Her daughter was in a pool of blood and she took her to Safdarjung Hospital.
3. Thereafter, IO along with HC Arvind reached at the spot and found the blood was scattered on the floor.
Crime Team was called at the spot, who inspected the spot.
IO prepared the tehrir and got the FIR registered in the instant case under Section 307/506 IPC.
Site plan was prepared at the instance FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC of complainant and exhibits were collected.
During investigation, accused Harikant Maan S/o. Sh. Jai Prakash was arrested and his disclosure statement was recorded.

Weapon of offence was recovered at the instance of accused from the bushes of a vacant plot, Gaushala Road Kishangarh towards Fish Park, pointing out memo recovery as well as sketch of sword was prepared.
Accused was sent to JC.

During further investigation,
statement of victim Ms. Ritika under Section 161 Cr.PC was recorded alleging that she was having affair with accused Harikant Maan and on 23.05.2018, at about 7:00 p.m., he came to meet her and asked to elope and marry him otherwise, he will kill her.
She started crying and asked to to leave otherwise she will raise alarm and call the police.
Thereafter, he left the spot in anger and threatened with dire consequences.
She further alleged that at about 10:30 p.m., accused Harikant Maan called him on his phone and asked to meet outside the lobby of her house to which she refused.
He again and again called her but she did not agree to meet her and finally accused called her to get some water for him.
When she went there, accused again threatened her and took out a sword from the bed lying on the lobby and stabbed on her stomach.
In the meanwhile, on hearing her voice, her mother came out and accused threatened her mother and run away from the spot.
4. After completion of investigation, the charge-sheet was filed for the offence punishable under Section 307/506 IPC against accused before the concerned Court.

Charge:
5. Charge for the offence punishable under Section 307/506 IPC was framed against the accused, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC  The Trial Prosecution evidence :

To bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined 14 witnesses at all.

PW-1 Ms. Kavita Giri ( Complainant); PW-2 Ms. Ritika (Injured); PW-3 SI Ajay (Incharge Crime Team);
PW-4 Ms. Divya (Public Witness); PW-5 HC Braham Prakash (Photographer); PW-6 HC Arvind (Witness of investigation); PW-7 Dr. Mohit Kumar Patralekh (Regarding MLC of injured); PW-8 W/HC Gomati Dhayal (Witness of investigation); PW-9 SI H. Gangte (Investigating Officer); PW-10 Dr. Anirban Das (Discharge Summary of injured); PW-11 Dr. Arundev (Regarding nature of injury);
PW-12 Ms. Manisha Upadhyay (FSL Expert); PW-13 Sh. Parveen Kumar, Nodal Officer, Reliance Jio Ltd (CDR and CAF of mobile number complainant) and PW-14 Sh. Pawan Singh, Nodal Officer,
Vodafone Idea Ltd. (CDR, Cell ID and CAF of mobile number of complainant).
The relevant portion of their testimonies are discussed under the succeeding paragraphs.

7. PW-1 Smt. Kavita Giri deposed that she along with her daughter namely Ritika and son Abhishek was residing at 72 M, third floor, Vasant Vihar, CPWD Colony, New Delhi; that one day in the month of May 2018 at about 7.00 pm accused Hari Kant Maan came to her house to meet her daughter and talked to her for some time and went away from there; that at about 10.30 pm accused again came to her house and told that he wants to talk to Ritika who was present alongwith her cousin namely Divya in her bedroom, Ritika came out from the bedroom and started talking with the accused in veranda; that after 15/20 minutes she heard loud voices and when she came out of the room and peeped out from the main door (jaaliwala), she saw that accused was taking out a sword like object from the stomach of her daughter and she also saw her daughter FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC bending holding her stomach, she heard accused saying 'main dekh loonga'
and then he ran away with sword like object; that she came outside the main gate and took her daughter inside where she fell unconscious; that her cousin Divya came out of the room and called ambulance which came after 15/20 minutes and Ritika was taken to Safdarjung Hospital; that when she was in the hospital she started receiving calls of accused on her phone who asked her whether she had made a call to police or not.
She further deposed that her daughter was treated in the hospital and in the meantime the police from the hospital as well as area police also come there and inquired from her.
Her statement was recorded which is Ex PW-1/A.

She further deposed that the police visited her house and inspected the spot, the blood stains from the tiles were lifted and the chuni/dupatta which Ritika had wrapped around her stomach after injury was handed over by her cousin Divya to police; that police inspected the spot and site plan was prepared Ex PW-1/B, spot was also got photographed; that her daughter remained admitted at Safdarjung hospital till 02.06.2018.
The witness has correctly identified the accused in the court.
She further deposed that accused was her children's friend for about 05 years prior to the incident who left their neighbourhood to Vasant Kunj but kept on visiting them.
7.1 The witness was cross examined by Ld APP who suggested that incident is of 23.05.2018 and the witness stated to be correct.

Witness has also correctly identified the case property i.e. one sword having brass handle and iron made blade as well as one orange & red printed chunni, which has been proved as Ex.PW-2/P1 and Ex PW-2/P2 respectively.
7.2 During cross examination, witness stated that her statement was recorded by the IO on 23.05.2018 in the hospital.

She admitted that her flat No. 72-M was surrounded by other flats also,
which were occupied except one flat at third floor and on the date of incident, she was having his mobile No. 8744892443 in FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC her possession.

3
Her niece called the police on No. 100 and ambulance as well and disclosed the name of accused/assailant.
They reached the hospital at about 11:00 p.m.
She admitted that it is not recorded in her statement Ex.PW1/A that accused had called her 4-5 times, however, voluntarily stated that she had told the IO about the same.
In these calls, accused inquired whether, she had called the police and that he was at his house.
Accused also extended threats to kill his son and she immediately informed the same to IO.
She stated that her daughter was not conscious at the time when she was being provided medical aid at Safdarjung Hospital.
Again said, she was not completely unconscious but was still disoriented.
She regain her consciousness on the next day after operation and her statement was recorded by the IO on 31.05.2018 in her presence at her residence.
Even statement of her niece Diksha was recorded on 31.05.2018 for the first time.
She admitted that accused used to visit her house quite often even in her absence.
She also admitted that accused is married and his wife had filed some divorce case pending before the Court.
She also admitted that it was not within her knowledge that her daughter Ritika had gone to Jaipur with accused on 18.03.2018 or had stayed there till 21.03.2018.
Her daughter had celebrated her birthday on 20.03.2018 in Delhi, however, no photographs were taken as the celebration was a private affair.
She stated that accused had told her that he had come to see her daughter when she had opened the door for him and he was not carrying any weapon with him at that time.
She admitted that neither she nor her niece raised alarm after seeing Ritika having been stabbed by the accused.
She stated that there was no question of intervening by them as accused left immediately after stabbing and no neighbour had gathered in their house.
She further stated that the quarrel had started suddenly between the accused and her daughter which lasted for 10-15 minutes.
She had not called the police regarding the said quarrel.
Vol. It was not of such nature so as to call the FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC police.
Neither she nor her niece Diksha tried to intervene in the said quarrel.
She stated that she cannot tell when, where and by whom her signatures on Ex.PW1/B were obtained.

7.3 In further cross examination, she stated that her mobile No. 8744892443 is of Idea Service Provider and same is registered in her name and she had not made any call to the accused after the incident.

She further stated that people in the locality take a stroll in the night time from 9:30 p.m.
to 10:30 p.m. and she did not call anyone in the locality or from the neighbourhood to apprehend the accused after the incident.
She admitted that the clothes worn by her daughter Ritika were torn after the stab injury and the said clothes were changed by her in the hospital.
The said clothes were not handed over to anyone by her and were thrown when instructed by the Nurse/Attendant in the hospital.
She stated that on 24.05.2018, she did not visit her home and remained in the hospital throughout.
She further stated that the blood was lifted by the police from the living room in her presence.
Accused had taken the sword with him.
She further stated that no writing work was done by the IO at the time of removing the blood stained tiles from her home and her signatures were not obtained by the IO at that time.
She further stated that accused had not told her that he wanted to marry with Ritika and Ritika also never told her that accused is pressurizing her to marry him.

She stated that she stated in her statement Ex.PW1/A that she had seen the accused taking out the sword from the abdomen of her daughter and that she had also seen her daughter bending while holding her stomach (Confronted with Ex.PW1/A wherein it is not recorded verbatim).
She had also told the IO in her statement that she had seen the accused threatening her daughter that he will see her (Confronted with Ex.PW1/A wherein it is not so recorded).

She also stated that she had told the IO State vs Hari Kant Mann on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79732368/
4 that when she was in hospital, she started receiving calls from the accused or that these FIR No.
167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC calls, he had asked her whether police had been called or that he had threatened her to kill her son (Confronted with Ex.PW1/A wherein it is not so recorded).
8. PW-2 Ritika/ victim deposed that she knew the accused who was his friend for last 05 years being his neighbour; that on 23.05.2018 in the evening she alongwith her mother and cousin Divya were present at home and at about 7.00 pm accused Harikant Maan came to her place to meet her and asked her to marry him and to run away with him otherwise he will kill her ( mujhse shaadi kar ley,
mere sath bhag chal warna jaan se maar doonga ), she asked him to go from there and not to annoy her and the accused left her place in anger saying 'main tujhe dekh loonga aur kahika nahi chodunga'; that at about 10.30 pm accused made a call to her and asked her to come to the corridor to meet him to which she refused but accused repeatedly called her and also asked her for water saying that he was thirsty, she took water for him in corridor where accused again threatened her and asked her to marry him and on refusal, he stabbed her a sword into her abdomen saying that he will kill her and on hearing her voice her mother came out, the accused also threatened her mother to kill her and he ran away from the spot alongwith the sword.

8.1 The witness identified the case property i.e. one sword with brass handle and iron made blade already Ex PW-2/P1 and one chunni of orange and red print which she stated that the same belongs to her mother, already Ex PW-2/P2. 8.2 During cross examination, the witness has been shown the photocopy of an undated handwritten statement brought by Ld. Defence Counsel and the witness admits the statement to have been made by her in her own handwriting.
Said statement is Ex.PW2/DA.
Witness stated that she cannot say as to whether her said statement was recorded after one or two months of his discharge from the hospital.
Vol. Same was recorded after few days of her discharge from the FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC hospital.
Except the statement Ex.PW2/DA, no other statement of her recorded by the police during the entire investigation of the case.
She admitted that accused Harikant Maan was her close friend being neighbour and she was not having any love affair with him.
Till the day of incident, she and the accused were having cordial relations.
She admitted that accused was married and was having a daughter and he was staying with his family consisting of parents, wife and child.
The accused never proposed her for marriage, but he had said in the year 2014 that he used to like her.
She stated that accused never asked her to accompany him for the purpose of marrying him.
Her birthday falls on 20th March and she along with her brother and and accused Harikant Maan had celebrated her birthday in a hotel at Jaipur.
She stated that on 23.05.2018, when accused had come firstly at 7:00 p.m., her mother was present at home and accused has stayed for about half an hour at that time.
It was for the first time that accused asked her to marry him at that time.
Her mother was not present at that place in the house, however, she told her mother that accused asked her to marry with him.
She further stated that during 15-20 minutes, the accused was forcing her to accompany him and to marry with him and she was telling him that he is already married.
The said conversation was in loud voice and she did not call her mother or cousin when accused was forcing her.
She further stated that their flat is located on 3rd floor surrounded by other flats, which are occupied except one and none of the neighbour came hearing their loud conversation.

She stated that she had told in her State vs Hari Kant Mann on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79732368/

(Confronted with statement Ex.PW2/DA, where the factum of taking out the weapon from under the pillow is not mentioned).
She stated that no blood was oozed/fell in the gallery because she had pressed the wound.
Few neighbours were also present when she was taken to the hospital.
She told the name of FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC accused to the police after 02 days of her operation.

9. IO recorded his statement.

9.1 During cross examination, witness stated that the crime had been committed inside the room of the flat and he found the blood stained chunni lying on the floor and IO did not ask him to inspect the gallery in front of Flat No. 72-M, CPWD Colony, Vasant Vihar, and also the stair-case.
He further stated that when he entered the flat, the IO pointed out that the incident had taken place inside the flat and he asked him to inspect the place where the blood was lying.
The blood was lying on the floor immediately after the entrance of the flat.

Ms Divya (cousin of the victim) deposed that in the year 2018 she was staying at the house of Smt. Kavita Giri who was sister-in-law ( nanad) of her bua; she was studying B.Sc (botany) Hons in Dayal Singh College at that time; that on 23.05.2018 she was studying in the back room as there was her exam on next day; that in the evening of 23.05.2018 accused Hari Kant came and had some conversation with her cousin Ritika and left after some time and

again at 10.30 pm Ritika went out in verandah to meet accused and on hearing noise of quarrel, she came out of bedroom and saw that blood was oozing out FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC from the abdomen of Ritika and her aunt Kavita was holding Ritika, so she got scared.
They tied dupatta around the wound at abdomen and took her to Safdarjung Hospital at 11/11.30 pm.
10.1 During cross examination, she stated that she had not stated in her statement to the police that she saw accused Harikant Maan running with a sword in his hand.
She further stated that her statement was never recorded during investigation for the first she has tendered her statement in the Court on 16.01.2020.
She further stated that the blood of the victim of was lying on the floor inside the flat where the incident took place.

18.1 During cross examination, witness admitted that the place of occurrence is situated in a gated colony of CPWD but he did not find any chowkidar on duty.

It is a fundamental doctrine of criminal law that the onus to prove its case lies on the prosecution.
Thus, in a criminal trial, the onus to prove the commission of offence by the accused is always upon the prosecution and the same never shifts upon the accused.
The prosecution has to establish before the Court that the accused had committed the offence beyond shadow of all reasonable doubts.

Brief facts of the case :
1. The accused has been facing trial of the charge that on 23.05.2018 in between 10:30 p.m. to 11:00 p.m., he stabbed the injured Ritika by sword FIR No. 167/2018 PS - Vasant Vihar U/s. -307/506 IPC causing grievous injury with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that if by that act he had caused the death of injured Ritika, he would have been guilty of murder and also intimidated the complainant as well as injured Ritika by threatening to kill the injured Ritika.
Investigation conducted and statement of injured:
2. On 24.05.2018, on receipt of DD No. 5A regarding MLC No. 124146, IO along with HC reached at Safdarjang Hospital and as per the MLC doctor declared the patient Ms. Reetika D/o.
Her daughter Reetika leaving her cousin Divya in bedroom started talking to Harikant Maan in Varandha.
House of the door was opened and after sometime, on hearing quarrel noise between accused Harikant Maan and her daughter Reetika, she went to the door and saw that accused Harikant Maan @ Aashu stabbed her daughter Reetika on her abdomen with a sword type weapon and threatened her and run away from the spot.
IO prepared the tehrir and got the FIR registered in the instant case under Section 307/506 IPC.
During investigation, accused Harikant Maan S/o. Sh. Jai Prakash was arrested and his disclosure statement was recorded.
During further investigation,
statement of victim Ms. Ritika under Section 161 Cr.PC was recorded alleging that she was having affair with accused Harikant Maan and on 23.05.2018, at about 7:00 p.m., he came to meet her and asked to elope and marry him otherwise, he will kill her.
When she went there, accused again threatened her and took out a sword from the bed lying on the lobby and stabbed on her stomach.
In the meanwhile, on hearing her voice, her mother came out and accused threatened her mother and run away from the spot.

As per the case of the prosecution, the alleged incident had taken place in the veranda and accused allegedly took out the sword lying under the pillow on the bed placed by the complainant in the veranda.
A site plan is crucial in criminal cases as it helps the Court visualize the scene, verify witness testimonies, and establish the mens rea (intention) and actus reus (physical act) of the accused.
It physically maps where the accused attacked and where the victim stood, helping to verify the probability of the prosecution's story.
47. Law is well settled that preparation of site plan is not merely a procedural formality but a crucial instrument for reaching a just conclusion.
In the instant case, the gallery/ veranda which is the spot of incident or/and the bed kept in the said gallery/varanda from where the alleged weapon of offence was taken out, have not shown in the site plan prepared by the Investigating Officer.
The omission to show them in site plan cannot be attributed to a mere lapse on the part of the investigating agency specially when Investigating Officer himself during his cross examination categorically stated that " It is correct that in site plan Ex.PW1/B, I have not reflected the gallery where the alleged incident is stated to have taken place.".
Even perusal of the site plan Ex.PW1/B by the Court shows that the only colony as a whole and the surrounding area has been shown in the same and it is not even that the spot was inside or outside the flat of the complainant.
As per the case of the prosecution itself, the accused was arrested in the morning of next date of incident after he had hidden the alleged weapon of offence in the bushes opposite the park but was wearing the same t-shirt having blood stains which he was wearing at the time of offence.
This fact putforth by the prosecution seems to be unreasonable and does not clear the test of normal prudence, as if the accused had the time to hide the alleged weapon, he also had time to change or throw his blood stained cloths/t-shirt.
Even otherwise FSL result is only an opinion which has to be corroborated with material particulars.
The non-seizure of clothes of the injured stated to be worn by her at the time of stabbing on the abdomen also dents the case of the prosecution.
